change: Photo ID for any "non-verifiable" FOIA submitter now; says it "will soon move to requiring ID for all submissions". No posted policy found.

Agencies may run portals with CAPTCHA, physical-address verification and an Indiana-residency check; may deprioritize and surcharge out-of-state and automated requests; may decline suspected data-scraping or phishing requests; must report suspected automated requests to the Public Access Counselor.
source_kind: primary (statute text from the Public Access Counselor)

change: A public body that reasonably believes a request was not submitted by a person may require the requester to verify orally or in writing that they are a person; it may not require identifying information such as a photo ID.
source_kind: primary (Attorney General PAC newsletter quoting the statute)

change: "Person" under the Public Records Act and open-meeting laws excludes AI systems, autonomous agents and robots; a human using AI at ordinary volume keeps full rights; agencies may use a verification tool. Effective 2027-01-01.
source_kind: secondary (law-firm alert; official site blocked automated reading)

change: Would have let custodians require government photo ID with an address as proof of Kentucky residency.
Would have limited right-to-know requests to New Hampshire residents with proof (press exempt).
Would let agencies deny requests on "reasonable suspicion" they were generated by AI or a script.
Would have required enough identifying information to verify the requester and ended anonymous requests.
Moved all open-records requests to a JustFOIA portal and stopped accepting requests by email.
Requests must be made in person or by certified mail when staff cannot authenticate the requester.
Hardcopy requests by mail or in person only; AI-generated requests not processed.
Prepayment when costs are expected and "safeguards against mass or AI-generated requests".
Surcharge for out-of-state and automated requests, residents first, and authority for the clerk to adopt identity verification requirements (under HEA 1360).
Implements HEA 1360 "to limit spam, phishing and bot requests".
Posts the 3(j) procedure: suspected AI or bot requesters must prove they are a real person by letter or phone.
